newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 11.

text.p: No evidence of crime by Morgan, says SFO: The Serious Fraud Office has found no evidence that NZ First MP Tukoroirangi Morgan acted criminally at Aotearoa Television Network. Page 1.
Absent MP may be about to quit party: Alliance MP Alamein Kopu may be about to quit her party after being absent from Parliament without permission for the past three days. Page 1.

Compulsory super running cost up to $20m a year: The government would spend $12 to $20 million a year more to administer compulsory superannuation, independent referendum panel chairman Sir John Robertson said on Thursday. Page 2.

Labour MP plans bill to set up judicial commission: Labour MP Dianne Yates is planning a private member's bill to set up a judicial commission responsible for judges' appointments and discipline procedures. Page 2.

More privacy protection sought: Privacy Commissioner Bruce Slane has called for an amendment to the Official Information Act to protect people who might be harrassed if identified in information made public. Page 2.

Economic slowdown 'may be longer': The slowdown that started in the New Zealand economy in the March quarter has the potential to be "deeper and longer than expected", according to a report by Hongkong and Shangai Banking Corporation. Page 15.
Most Kiwis aware of referendum: Most New Zealanders are well aware of the referendum on the proposed compulsory superannuation scheme, but there are some misconceptions about the scheme. Page 15.

Andrews pleased with FCL board's confidence: Fletcher Challenge executive Michael Andres is "extremely pleased" that after months of interviews the board showed sufficient confidence in him to appoint him as chief executive to succeed Hugh Fletcher. Page 16.

Sky forecast to produce a profit: Sky Television should turn its first profit in 1997, says Independent Newspapers managing director Mike Robson, negotiating to buy 51 percent of the pay TV company. Page 16.
ANZCO make move on meat restructure: The former Meat Board subsidiary ANZCO is tipped to buy Benmore Products in a move likely to trigger more industry restructuring.
Strong bidding sees yields fall to record low: The yield on November 2006 government stock fell to a new low on Thursday after the first government tender for the new financial year was snapped up.
TVNZ signs up for Internet exposure: TVNZ is the first New Zealand organisation to sign with Microsoft as an "active channel" on the next version of its Internet browser software.

Tower head dismisses super savings scheme: Tower Corporation, one of New Zealand's largest superannuation fund managers, has come out against the compulsory savings scheme unveiled by Treasurer Winston Peters on Monday.

Phillips' counsel claims Crown had mind-set: Former Pacer Kerridge executive chairman David Phillips' counsel, Gary Judd QC, told the jury at Phillip's fraud trial on Thursday that prosecution 10 years after the event came from the Crown's inability to admit a mistake.

Asian Props moves passed by meeting: Asian Properties shareholders took just 14 minutes on Thursday to agree to proposals to reduce the company's capital and delist it from the New Zealand Stock Exchange. Page 16.
